messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Uncertain Privacy will become a thing of the past in some domains, yet legal protections and encryption make total disappearance unlikely. Uncertain
Implausible We will copy human consciousness to a computer by the early 2030s because mind uploading requires unresolved neuroscience, simulation, and philosophical problems. Implausible
Plausible Wireless Internet coverage could reach most remote surfaces by the 2030s via satellite, but underwater, caves, and dense interiors remain exceptions. Plausible
Likely Most practical forms of transport will eventually become electric as batteries, infrastructure, and policy improve, though some niche uses may remain non electric. Likely
Certain Some effects of climate change will be irreversible over human timescales, especially ice sheet loss and ecosystem die offs, though outcomes still depend on mitigation. Certain
Unlikely Physical money may fade in many rich societies, but complete global disappearance of coins and notes is unlikely because cash serves privacy, resilience, and informal economies. Unlikely
Speculative Scientists may greatly extend healthy human life spans, but genetic immortality or century long life remains speculative and faces aging, entropy, and governance barriers. Speculative
